subject: Research request: FBI file 105-9673 ("Kohler, Walter"), RG 65, Box 156
body:
Dear reference staff,

I run a small open project on unsolved historical ciphers. I direct it and send its letters myself; AI agents (Claude models) do the archival searches and the checking, every step logged in the repository linked below. We are studying Walter Koehler, an Abwehr agent whom the FBI ran as a double agent. A German teleprinter letter of February 1944 to the Abwehr's Paris radio station ("Abwehrleitstelle Frankreich, Paris Funkstelle") quotes five enciphered messages about him, printed by David Kahn in Cryptologia 5(2) (1981), and we have not been able to read them. Nor have we found a published account of how these five were enciphered; Hoover's 1946 account describes a prayer-book cipher for the FBI-controlled channel to Hamburg, which may or may not apply here.

In NARA's own released FBI name-index material (the FBI Class Name Index and the 2004 Nazi War Crimes Disclosure Act list of released files) we found an entry for an FBI headquarters file on "Kohler, Walter": RG 65, Class 105, File 9673, Section 001 (and a second section, "EBF 003"), Box 156, location 230 86/16/05; the second section appears only in the name index. We have not found an item-level catalogue record for this file online and do not know what it contains.

Two questions: (1) can staff tell, from the file description or a quick look, whether it discusses Koehler's February 1944 Paris radio traffic or how it was enciphered; and (2) if it does, what would it cost to have the relevant pages copied. I understand this may need a formal reference request or a FOIA request, and I am happy to follow whichever route is right.

What we have on this, including the search log, is at https://github.com/NoAutopilot/cipher-lab/tree/main/ciphers/koehler-1944

[SIGN-OFF]
